fields.documented_meaning: The PayPal-generated ID for the captured payment.
fields.note: Identifier only: used for provenance references, the case id and (by equality only) dispute linkage.

fields.documented_meaning: Status of the captured payment; each value is described (COMPLETED = funds credited to the payee's PayPal account; PARTIALLY_REFUNDED / REFUNDED = refunded to the payer; PENDING, DECLINED, FAILED). Per-value meanings are in api_semantics.
fields.note: No current rule consumes payment status. Refund states are not reflected in the engine.

fields.documented_meaning: Reason a capture is PENDING or DENIED; includes BUYER_COMPLAINT (payer disputed with PayPal) and CHARGEBACK (funds reversed after the payer disputed with the issuer).
fields.note: Observation only. It is present only for some statuses and is not read as a dispute route.

fields.documented_meaning: Decimal string; the capture's total amount (item_total + tax + shipping + handling + insurance - discounts when a breakdown is given); must be positive.
fields.engine_consumer: engine.snad_exposure (the Phase 1 rule treats it as a conservative lower bound of exposure)
fields.note: Recorded as 'original transaction value' in the exposure view and NOT handed to the engine. PayPal documents that a dispute's amount may be less than the original transaction's gross or net amount, so the capture amount is not a minimum disputed exposure. Changing the engine's treatment needs a separately reviewed policy change.

fields.documented_meaning: Three-character ISO-4217 currency code.
fields.note: Handed over as a label. PayPal's Dispute Detail report documents that a disputed currency matches the original payment's currency.

fields.documented_meaning: The level of protection offered as defined by PayPal Seller Protection for Merchants. Optional object.

API semantics (documented, see api_semantics.py): whether the transaction is eligible for seller protection. ELIGIBLE = the seller's PayPal balance remains intact if the customer claims they did not receive an item or the account holder claims they did not authorize the payment; PARTIALLY_ELIGIBLE = item-not-received only; NOT_ELIGIBLE = not eligible for seller protection.
fields.note: The API meaning is recorded in the API-semantics layer. Equivalence with the Transaction Details eligibility mark that the legal policy names is NOT established: no PayPal document links them, the descriptions concern the PayPal balance, the policy says PayPal decides at dispute time, and another PayPal surface (the Dispute Detail report) describes a similarly named value with different scope. The token is therefore passed to the engine unchanged and opaque.

fields.documented_meaning: Array of conditions covered for the transaction; documented values ITEM_NOT_RECEIVED, UNAUTHORIZED_TRANSACTION.
fields.note: Observed and preserved. No engine fact or consumer exists for it; adding one would be new policy interpretation.

fields.documented_meaning: Typed only as a currency+amount ('money'); no primary doc retrieved states what it represents.
fields.note: An engine fact name exists, but equating them from the field NAME is the inference the rules forbid.

fields.documented_meaning: Documented only as an RFC 3339 date-time; which event each timestamp marks is not stated.
fields.note: Recorded raw. Not used for any window or timer (no such rule is modelled).

fields.documented_meaning: Appears in primary samples; no definition text retrieved this session.
fields.note: PayPal does not state that the order's shipping address IS the address on the Transaction Details page. Recorded (raw plus a key-renamed candidate) and never handed to the engine.

fields.documented_meaning: A key naming the payment source type appears in samples; no definition retrieved.
fields.note: The type key does not say whether a wallet payment was funded by card, bank or balance, which is what funding_source means.

fields.documented_meaning: The retrieved capture definition has no field exposing the funding instrument of a wallet payment.
fields.note: funding_source stays missing; the engine reports it as an open UNKNOWN.

fields.path: merchant account country (independently verified PayPal account data)
fields.documented_meaning: PayPal documents a partner-only 'show seller status' call (needs the ACCESS_MERCHANT_INFORMATION permission) whose sample response includes country and primary_currency. What 'country' denotes, and whether a direct-merchant integration can call it, was not established.
fields.note: Not implemented. Jurisdiction is merchant-asserted (MERCHANT_INPUT / MERCHANT_ASSERTED) or missing, never presented as PayPal-verified.

fields.documented_meaning: Appears in create-order REQUEST samples (merchant-declared); response behaviour not checked.
fields.note: Merchant-declared, not a PayPal observation.

fields.documented_meaning: Appear in samples; no definition retrieved.
fields.note: No current rule consumes payer data (data minimisation).

fields.documented_meaning: Enum of dispute reasons. Primary descriptions retrieved for MERCHANDISE_OR_SERVICE_NOT_RECEIVED (customer did not receive the merchandise or service) and UNAUTHORISED (customer did not authorize the purchase). No primary description retrieved for MERCHANDISE_OR_SERVICE_NOT_AS_DESCRIBED or the other values.
fields.note: Raw value always preserved. Normalised through CLAIM_REASON_TABLE_V1 only where established (NOT_RECEIVED, UNAUTHORISED); NOT_AS_DESCRIBED is not normalised yet; other reasons stay unknown.

fields.documented_meaning: The stage in the dispute lifecycle: INQUIRY, CHARGEBACK, PRE_ARBITRATION, ARBITRATION. Only INQUIRY has a retrieved description.
fields.note: Separate field. Never merged with reason or route; the engine has no lifecycle fact.

fields.documented_meaning: Where the customer created the dispute: INTERNAL (contacts PayPal), EXTERNAL (contacts their card issuer or bank), ALERT (pre-chargeback alert). PayPal's overview classes disputes as internal or external, and external includes card chargebacks and ACH returns.
fields.note: The only explicitly exposed and documented route-like field. INTERNAL -> PAYPAL_DISPUTE; EXTERNAL and ALERT are not normalised because external disputes include ACH returns, for which the retrieved policy establishes no Item Not Received handling. Never inferred from the claim reason.

fields.documented_meaning: The amount in the transaction that the customer originally disputed; may differ from the total gross or net amount of the original transaction (partial disputes).
fields.note: Held in the exposure view as 'disputed amount'. No engine consumer exists and none is added.

fields.documented_meaning: Appear in Disputes API samples; no definition retrieved.
fields.note: Used for linkage by identifier equality only: PayPal's docs do not state that a capture id and a seller_transaction_id share a namespace.

fields.documented_meaning: Enums and timestamps are listed; per-value meanings were not retrieved.
fields.note: Recorded raw; no consumer.

fields.documented_meaning: PayPal notifies the merchant of dispute events; CREATED includes the dispute id. Notifications carry a signature verified through POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature (five transmission headers; verification_status SUCCESS or FAILURE).
fields.note: Trigger only: a verified notification requests a fresh Disputes API read; its payload yields no facts. No live verifier is built.

fields.path: Dispute Detail Custom report (case type/reason, Seller Protection, disputed amount)
fields.documented_meaning: Per-claim SFTP report rows for approved merchants: case type, reason, a Seller Protection column (Eligible / Partially Eligible Unauth Only / Ineligible), the disputed amount (may be below the transaction amount) and the disputed transaction id.
fields.note: Supplementary / reconciliation source only. Not a dependency of any assessment.

fields.path: Transaction Search API (protection_eligibility etc.) and the Transaction Details page label
fields.documented_meaning: Not retrieved. The policy text itself refers to the label on the Transaction Details page.
fields.note: Possibly the only place the policy's own eligibility label is exposed; unchecked.

ELIGIBLE = the seller's PayPal balance remains intact if the customer claims they did not receive an item or the account holder claims they did not authorize the payment; PARTIALLY_ELIGIBLE = item-not-received only; NOT_ELIGIBLE = not eligible for seller protection.

Enum of dispute reasons. Primary descriptions retrieved for MERCHANDISE_OR_SERVICE_NOT_RECEIVED (customer did not receive the merchandise or service) and UNAUTHORISED (customer did not authorize the purchase). No primary description retrieved for MERCHANDISE_OR_SERVICE_NOT_AS_DESCRIBED or the other values.
